messages:
maya: Heads up — since ~04:10 UTC a bunch of GPU daemonset pods in us-west1 are stuck Pending. Autoscaler didn't add nodes. Noticed increased 502s from batch jobs :frowning:

sam: Can you paste the describe output? Which pod is pending exactly?

maya: pod infra-gpu-sidecar-7f9c (daemonset) -> describe shows: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  2s (x10 over 3m)  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 6 node(s) didn't match node selector, 6 node(s) had insufficient gpu resources.
```
Seems weird because we have a GPU pool; scale-bot shows no scale events.

igor: quick checks: are the GPU nodes labeled highmem=true? Daemonset has a nodeSelector in the manifest: `nodeSelector: { highmem: "true" }`. Our gpu-nodepool uses `gpu: "true"` + `accelerator: nvidia-a100`. No highmem label. So DS can't land on GPU pool and the regular pools don't have GPUs. :facepalm:

aisha: oh nice catch. Why didn't autoscaler add a GPU nodepool? CA will only scale nodepools when unschedulable pods match a nodepool's labels. Here the DS selectors exclude the GPU pool so CA sees no candidate and doesn't scale. Also check the node pool min/max — gpu-pool max is currently 0 (we disabled it last week for cost). scale-bot logs: `autoscaler: pool gpu-a100-usw1 max=0 min=0`.

sam: so two problems: (1) gpu nodepool scaled to 0, (2) daemonset nodeSelector mismatched labels. Quick mitigation: remove nodeSelector from daemonset so it can land on any highmem node (if those have GPUs) OR add highmem=true to gpu nodepool. Which is safer short-term?

maya: short-term I'd rather add label to gpu nodepool so daemonset lands on dedicated GPU hardware (we don't want infra sidecars on non-gpu nodes). But we need to bump gpu pool max >0 so CA can bring nodes. I'll open a tiny infra change.

igor: also double-check resource requests: these sidecars request `limits: { nvidia.com/gpu: 1 }`. If we flip to MIG or fractional slices later, the device-plugin could fragment resources making binpacking worse. For now integer GPU request is fine but watch for fragmentation when we add mixed MIG workloads.

aisha: created change CL-2412: label `highmem=true` on nodepool `gpu-a100-usw1` and set max=3. Deployed via infra CI -> will apply in ~2m. scale-bot: will report if CA triggers.

scale-bot: [automated] nodepool/gpu-a100-usw1 labels updated: +highmem=true, autoscaler.max updated 0->3

scale-bot: [automated] cluster-autoscaler event: scale-up triggered for nodepool gpu-a100-usw1, adding 1 node (reason: 4 unschedulable pods match pool labels)

maya: great, pods are starting to schedule! seeing `Status: Running` on 7/7 sidecars. :tada: We should follow up with a short postmortem and an ops playbook to avoid having gpu pools with max=0 for >24h.

sam: Agreed. Action items: (1) postmortem with timeline + CA config audit, (2) add alert for nodepool.max==0 when there are pending gpu pods, (3) doc note about nodeSelector vs nodepool labels. I'll own the alert. :thumbsup:

igor: also add a note to watch for binpacking when mixed request sizes arrive. If someone starts launching a bunch of tiny GPU tasks (MIG slices) we should surface fragmentation metrics (free-gpu-fragments per node) in console.

maya: Thanks all. Closing thread after postmortem stub created.
